scope: Public primary pages re-read in this stage; no tools downloaded, executed or sent to camera.

sources.observed: FX3 7.02 reverse-engineering request, opened Oct13; page still shows zero replies. This page supplies no flashing or recovery acceptance.
sources.limit: One discussion and scoped search, not proof that no FX3 work exists elsewhere. Battery allegations in the post are not adopted as fact.

sources.observed: Browser page marks A7C II Tools3.0.3, released Oct23, Latest; release describes USB read-error handling and interrupted-install resumption.
sources.limit: Author release claims for A7CII, not FX3 protocol, compatibility or recovery proof. REST metadata requests were rate-limited and exact new commit was not verified.

sources.observed: Users report no boot and repeating lamp pattern after installation. Oct25 comment describes re-entering through unaffected movie mode and then application-level restoration; Oct26 another user reports success.
sources.limit: User reports, not controlled independent recovery validation. The route depends on functioning application/mode code and must not be promised for FX3 movie-chain changes.

sources.observed: Current main README describes A7IV serial bootROM entry and a fastboot payload for eMMC partition backup/restoration; transparent dump/flash crypto explicitly has a boot0 exception.
sources.limit: A7IV-specific source. No FX3 execution, wiring, boot-ROM, crypto or same-body restoration acceptance established here.

sources.observed: mmap maps into the process virtual address space and returns the mapping address, with the object offset supplied separately.
sources.limit: Supports the generic mapping ABI interpretation; actual FX3 device-driver mapping and runtime addresses remain unobserved.

conclusion: Reviewed sources do not establish an independent FX3 rescue route for the intended MAIN modification. Retain same-body backup, limited restoration/readback and independent-entry gates.
